source: I'm going to town as soon as I can. I need a drink. And if you dare tell anyone you saw me leaving the castle, I'll slit your damn throat.
And don't you dare follow me there, either!
...I'm no fool.
(...She still doesn't trust me. I wonder if there's something more I can do. My brother mentioned Horatio and Gertrude.)
I'll be departing now.
You won't tell Father, will you?
You won't tell anyone, will you?
Let's both agree to pretend this never happened.
Right. That's... probably for the best.
Lady Ophelia. There's to be a betrothal announcement for Lady Brit and Prince Hamlet in the chapel anon.
Right now?
Yes. Admittedly, it is rather sudden.
Nevertheless, I've come to collect you—it would be inappropriate for you to miss this affair.
Lead the way.
Lady Ophelia. There's to be a betrothal announcement for Lady Brit and Prince Hamlet here shortly.
The others will be here in just a moment.
My thanks for your prompt attendance, everyone.
Without further ado, we've something proud to announce.
My nephew Prince Hamlet and Lady Birgitta are to be betrothed today.
In light of Lady Birgitta settling into her role within the court, we felt it was the right time to make such a match.
Now may Denmark be all the more strengthened by the union of our throne with one of our greatest noble houses.
My son Prince Hamlet and Lady Birgitta are to be betrothed today.
(Oh, God.)
A-ah, why hadn't I heard of this?
Never mind it... yes, never mind it. Pleasant news all around.
Bernardo, as the next-closest holy man amongst us, if you would do the honors?
My lord, are you certain you don't wish to wait for the castle chaplain to return from his countryside tour?
Absolutely certain, Bernardo.
I see. Then of course, my liege. I'll do my best.
My lady, are you certain you don't wish to wait for the castle chaplain to return from his countryside tour?
I see. Then of course, my lady. I'll do my best.
Let us all bear witness to the betrothal of Prince Hamlet of Denmark, and Lady Birgitta of House Brockenhuus.
Honor, riches, marriage, blessing, long continuance, and increasing hourly joys be still upon you.
Scarcity and want shall shun you.
Are there any who would provide testimony against this venerable union in the eyes of the law and of God Almighty?
My poor brother. His face is trembling.
I've long believed marriage to be a dead institution, but regardless: Best wishes.
Certainly none from me!
Hmph. Perhaps marriage will finally settle the boy's wild side. I support such a union.
Excellent. Then...
May the Lord bless this union and guide this couple in their path to marriage.
May He watch over them these coming weeks and keep their hearts and souls pure of sin.
And may we all remain in good health and good fortune to witness that union.
(They look miserable, too. I did this to them.)
(And as a result, Laertes' heart is breaking.)
(They look miserable. I did this to them.)
(I wonder what my brother would think.)
(I imagine he'd be suffering now, too.)
All is well. There shall be a wedding in several weeks' time!
What do you want?
I came to find you. I thought you might be out here.
Did you know this would happen?
Not precisely, but sort of.
I suspected. My father sent me to Elsinore to make a suitable match.
I was the last to know. As usual.
It happened so swiftly.
Listen, Hamlet. Neither of us were pleased to be in that chapel. I know how you still feel for Ophelia.
But perhaps there's some kind of arrangement we can broker. Some way we can both find happiness in this mess.
Large things are coming. Events larger than us both. And I fear for you.
You may be mad, but of the crimes of the others, you are innocent.
Surely we can work together within the confines of our matchmaking, no?
It's not that simple.
My country expects this of me. My mother—my father—my whole life I knew this would come to pass some day.
But I feel it bearing down on me, crushing me—
All of this...
What about my life? What about what I want?
I never asked to be here.
You don't understand what it's like to live under this kind of pressure.
You can never truly understand, and I can never truly explain.
I don't understand? Why, you--
You sniveling, spineless, self-absorbed, melodramatic, idiotic child!
You have no idea what I've been through. What I've had to do to be here today.
I hoped to come here to barter peace, but you can think of nothing beyond the end of your nose, can you?
In the end, I guess it doesn't really matter.
In a few short days, all your burdens shall be lifted from you, poor fool.
I suspect this betrothal shall be far more drawn-out than that.
That's not even remotely what I was referring to.
Then you speak in riddles.
No. You're just all too clueless to look beyond what's happening right here, in Elsinore.
And not even I can save you from that short-sightedness.
I realize that now.
I thought there might be a way to help. But it's useless to try.
Good night, Hamlet.
I hope you can find some small peace in the days ahead.
I've no time for this. No time to be lectured by you, or anyone else.
That idiot.
S-stupid bottle's nearly empty.
Laertes! There y'are.
We, er... well, Brit told us you might be upset. About the impending betrothal, that is.
We, er... well, we all saw the betrothal, of course.
We came to see if you were all right, lad.
Where did you get a bottle of rum in that size?
And perhaps more crucially, do you intend to drink the whole thing?
Don't ask, and yes.
She's going to marry him. She's going to be sharing a bed with him.
Low-lifed, small-pricked thief of a boy that he is!
Now, which girl is 'e all besotten over again?
Are you blind, Marcellus? Can you not see Cupid's radiant arrows fly? This is a battlefield!
Young Laertes here is deeply in love with Lady Birgitta. Who, as we all know, is a mite above his station.
Grrgh... My father's a Duke, though our coffers may be slim. Don't belittle my options.
Ah, titles. I never can remember them. Apologies, Young Laertes.
I wish you'd stop calling me that, too.
Calling you what, Young Laertes?
Come now. It's not all bad.
Besides, didn't Hamlet return your lute to you after all?
In fact, he never stole it in the first place. Perhaps there is a way to make amends.
He did. But that's not important.
Yes. It truly is.
H-he's going to take her to bed.
She'll bear his children, awful rotten creatures in their father's image...
He's going to treat her as foully as he did my sister.
He knows no kindness. He's petulant. Anxious.
No. He won't marry her.
Not if I have anything to say about it.
I have seen the light. When I was a child, I spoke like a child. But the time has come to put aside childish things.
My father would have wanted me to make this match.
No matter what I might desire, the kingdom comes first. That's the sort of King I want to be.
You and I both know this is the last thing we desired. And I've no intention of trying to court you, or turn your disgust to love.
But... you, too, understand the chess board we stand upon.
You need me for my father's support. I know.
With your father's men in my army, I will forge a new destiny for this country. Denmark shall become a feared military power. And soon, others will join us.
So are you ready? To become my bride, that is?
And I shall never be ready.
But if this is the way forward, then I must be.
Well then. We've announcements to make, haven't we?
Come, then.
Lady Brit, Hamlet—the time has long since come to get you two together.
My wife is champing at the bit to make a good match, as always.
Lady Birgitta, we've spoken with your father Soren already. He has given his word. You will be wed.
And with this union, Denmark's ties with our own local houses will grow to be more powerful than any previous King's.
Especially in light of my husband's passing. I know he would have wanted this.
Lady Birgitta, we've spoken with your father Soren already. As the de facto speaker for the noble houses, he has given his word. You will be wed.
My son, are you ready to become a man and take a wife?
Now? You're certain?
Mother, this is rather sudden.
I understand. And for that, I apologize. But Denmark must have a King upon the throne.
My dear Hamlet. If you do not take Lady Brit as your wife, then you and I will surely be ousted from Elsinore.
We no longer control the nobility. They will elect any successor they deem fit. This union is the best for all parties.
But truly, we should be grateful that Brit's father is so amenable to this marriage.
So... my son, are you ready?
No. I'm not. My heart belongs elsewhere. And I will not force it to withhold.
But Hamlet--
Enough. If I am to be King, I need to make my own decisions.
I made a promise to Ophelia that I would ensure our future was ours alone.
Unless she herself rejects me, my faith is with her. I apologize, Brit, but I cannot marry you.
This is very like my son.
He'll come around. I'm sure of it.
No. But Father would have wanted me to make this match.
What about you, Lady Brit? Will you take Hamlet as your God-given husband?
If that is your wish, my lady.
Brit. Listen.
I was not in love with Hamlet's father when I met him. I found him to be cold. Distant. Frightening. But I soon came to love him all the same.
Time can turn even the most unwilling heart to softness. Time will grow a boy into a husband worth honoring, or a girl into a proud wife.
And there is yet time for us all, now that peace has come to Elsinore.
Come. Celebrations must be made. Let us depart for now.
Well, it's fortunate for both of us, then, that you have no choice in the matter.
I hope this process might change your heart, my son.
This is the best possible thing for you and for Denmark. Some day you will understand I do this not to cause you pain, but out of love.
What about you, Brit? Will you take Hamlet as your God-given husband?
Wonderful. Now, Hamlet.
I was not in love with your father when I met him. I found him to be cold. Distant. Frightening. But I soon came to love him all the same.
